# Dust — a chosen ordinary life, useful skill, and unreliable protection

## Responsibility and evidence boundary

Dust is an independently motivated person whose current life in Axel has positive value. His former knightly identity explains particular skills, obligations, attachments, and concealments; it does not turn every current failure into a deliberate disguise. The useful account must preserve his opportunism and coercion alongside his practical intelligence, affection, and actual sacrifices. Neither the heroic past nor his unflattering self-description supplies the whole person.

This monograph draws on the already admitted and completed DUST01–07 and separate unnumbered DUST-CONT analyses, their source-specific corrections, and relevant MAIN01–17 and CONTEXP evidence. The current audit has received all eight Dust analytical reports. Direct Japanese rereception is confined to separately recorded member/paragraph windows; it is not a new complete traversal of every EPUB, ruby, image, or ancillary component. FD's game-novelization plane and other continuities remain qualified. Repeated scenes, alternate viewpoints, letters, dreams, retrospective accounts, and public heroic histories retain different evidential weights.

These are known sources. This is an expanded interpretation and a candidate basis for the separate operational model, not a new blind prediction or a revision of the seven original Dust questions. Those originals, their fourteen empty future fields, the principal models, and all historical scores remain exact. The private draft still requires its current ledger/event reconciliation and cohort review before canonical adoption.

## The ordinary self is wanted

The contrast between knight and delinquent is not adequately described as a noble essence hiding beneath disposable bad manners. Dust wants the companions, leisure, familiarity, and relative freedom of his present home. He can value a quiet life without living it quietly. His misconduct often concerns things he actually wants now: money, service access, drink, entertainment, advantage over acquaintances, or an escape from embarrassment. An old professional capacity does not make those motives insincere. (DUST01, especially C01 and Final; DUST05 U012; DUST07 U014; DUST-CONT §§11–13.)

DUST05 makes the distinction unusually concrete. After the dragon strikes him, Dust misidentifies Leen as the princess and narrates himself as the knight ライン・シェイカー. His formal 私 and sacrificial language belong to that altered appraisal. Leen objects that the Dust she knows survives through selfish and underhanded methods; the painful headbutt is followed by his own current name, rough speech, and rejection of the old pattern of brooding. The restored Dust then performs real protection and takes burns for Leen. The source therefore separates a mistaken knight/princess identification from a later protective act by the present person. It does not establish a clinical disorder, two independently existing people, or a cure of all conflicting attachments. (DUST05 U012 P574–641, particularly P591/P599/P602.)

The old name should remain complete and source-bound. ライン・シェイカー is not a reason to merge Dust with the princess's attendant Rain/Rein, whose レイン name and role are distinct. Rionor / リオノール and Leen / リーン are also different people. Resemblance, disguise, temporary substitution, and a confused identification are events to explain, not identity equivalences. DUST06 gives the princess's name and an attributable substitution history; DUST07 supplies deliberate disclosure of Dust's past and the dragon's identity to Taylor and Keith. Their prior suspicion of noble or knightly origins is explicitly weaker than their newly learned Dragon Knight identification. Their subsequent attempt to pretend they recognized the Leen/princess switch fails. (DUST06 U010 P596–640; DUST07 U011 P419–453.)

## Concealment has relational costs and a permission structure

Dust does not merely avoid a weapon because he lacks the ability to use it. The recalled instruction permits the spear for Rionor or another person he truly wants to protect. The complete alternatives matter. In DUST07 he recalls that instruction, privately identifies Leen, and adds companions, friends, and the town. He then chooses training and disclosure. This is an actual change in his current use of an existing constraint, rather than an exception invented by the analyst after a convenient victory. (DUST03 recalled instruction; DUST07 U011 P390–427.)

Privacy is more than a wish to look impressive. Dust hides the child's identity, experiences rumors and social costs, and initially searches alone. He eventually makes a particular request for help and receives it. The later relief after telling Taylor and Keith suggests a real burden of concealment, while their qualified recognition exposes his overestimate of how successfully he had hidden his history. Disclosure to those companions does not give every citizen, client, or enemy the same information. (DUST05 U012 P107–428; DUST07 U011 P419–453.)

Rionor's continuing importance does not make Leen a substitute who can be modeled entirely through the princess. Leen acts under her own knowledge, objects to imposed roles, and supplies her own reasons for later continuation. Her DUST06 viewpoint distinguishes initial capture, refusal of withdrawal, a later usable exit, and her renewed decision. The unnumbered continuation gives her a separate account of embarrassment, competence, connection, and wanting to benefit Dust. Those reasons are reader-accessible evidence about Leen; they need not already be known to Dust. (DUST06 U012 P427–597; DUST-CONT U012 P436–510.)

## Skill is real and distributed

Dust can read equipment, change encounter geometry, recruit providers, exploit an opponent's options, and use trained weapons. Those capacities are not discredited simply because he also makes bad decisions. Conversely, technical effectiveness cannot certify his treatment of the people whose labor makes a plan possible. The DUST02 machine confrontation needs Keith's rope, Taylor's shield, Yunyun's cut, Dust's spear, and Leen's Lightning. Penetration alone is not the completed stop. Later joint battles similarly require actual provider access, material resources, and opportunities created by others. (DUST01 C04/Final; DUST02 Final; DUST06 climax; DUST07 U013; DUST-CONT U014.)

The visible contrast between his unusual physical capacity, weaker ordinary sword performance, and older spear skill matters more than a scalar competence score. Missing weapons, healing, armor, reach, transport, and opposition can change the outcome. Borrowing a noble persona through finite equipment does not itself establish superior force, and asking a provider for help does not mean that provider's power has become his own. The helmeted admirer lends equipment for a day under stated conditions; those terms are neither a donation nor an observed completed return. (DUST03 U014 P244–350; DUST07 U011 P404–441.)

Success also has several endpoints. An attack can penetrate without completing rescue; a false report can recruit help without proving the report true; a chosen intervention can work while creating debt or collateral damage. The eventual weakening of the DUST07 enemy is observed locally, but the connection to the distant main-series victory is Dust's inference. Rouzeri's fall is not an individually performed death check. The account should preserve those limits rather than grant the local hero omniscient credit.

## Particular care does not provide a reliable ethical override

Dust's affection has behavioral content. Gifts, labor, asking for help, searching, remaining under danger, protecting Leen after the identity confusion ends, and adjusting care for the child all have actual costs. A mixed motive does not make such acts unreal. DUST07's final private recognition and actual hand pull also matter without completing a final romantic contract. The anticipated approach to a mouth is interrupted; the source does not show mouth contact. (DUST01 C02/Ep; DUST04 coat and care episodes; DUST05 U012 P314–723; DUST07 U014 P81–148.)

The converse is equally important: he sometimes knowingly obstructs or declines needed help. DUST02's forced attraction is contrary evidence about his regard for another person's refusal. In DUST03 he stops Yunyun's available rescue while guards are still being swallowed. DUST06 includes both deferred feasible inquiry in favor of drinks and teasing during the princess's immediate toad predicament, after which Yunyun performs the rescue. In DUST07 Dust and Taylor intentionally shut their eyes and ears during Keith's forced removal and the actual blast. These acts cannot be repaired by later protection, survival, amusement, or a claim that the danger needed first to cause bodily injury. (DUST02 C02 P149/P156–176/P420–424; DUST03 U013 P218–247; DUST06 §9; DUST07 U011 training/removal sequence.)

The earlier broad protective-override account must therefore remain rejected as a general rule. Not every omission is an equally complete trial of the exact old N01 conjunction: some scenes leave a competing leisure option or feasible protective means unresolved. That qualification preserves honest missingness; it does not erase directly shown coercion or create a new pure-motive requirement. In the unnumbered continuation, direct questions and patient care coexist with tolerated royal coercion, delayed recovery, and ignoring another person's fear. Concern inside his narration is not a substitute for the omitted action. (DUST-CONT U011/U013/U014; original N01 and current qualifications.)

His companions also cause harm. Coerced training can produce useful skill while retaining hidden purpose, a blocked exit, restraint, fear, and unwanted contact. Taylor's apology and money are separate later acts, not retroactive assent. Likewise, manager permission cannot supply Lolisa's consent, and the child's gratitude or partnership does not automatically authorize removal of body material. Treating Dust accurately requires the same actor-specific standards when he is recipient, instigator, accomplice, or helper.

## Money, rewards, and selective checking

Dust is neither an uninterested altruist nor uniformly incapable of checking a deal. He sometimes appropriates entrusted money despite knowing its ownership, commits before future access is secure, invents inducements, or changes moral appraisal when his share improves. DUST04's promised multiplication does not undo the appropriation or prove repayment. # Dust — a chosen ordinary life, useful skill, and unreliable protection

## Responsibility and evidence boundary

Dust is an independently motivated person whose current life in Axel has positive value. His former knightly identity explains particular skills, obligations, attachments, and concealments; it does not turn every current failure into a deliberate disguise. The useful account must preserve his opportunism and coercion alongside his practical intelligence, affection, and actual sacrifices. Neither the heroic past nor his unflattering self-description supplies the whole person.

This monograph draws on the already admitted and completed DUST01–07 and separate unnumbered DUST-CONT analyses, their source-specific corrections, and relevant MAIN01–17 and CONTEXP evidence. The current audit has received all eight Dust analytical reports. Direct Japanese rereception is confined to separately recorded member/paragraph windows; it is not a new complete traversal of every EPUB, ruby, image, or ancillary component. FD's game-novelization plane and other continuities remain qualified. Repeated scenes, alternate viewpoints, letters, dreams, retrospective accounts, and public heroic histories retain different evidential weights.

These are known sources. This is an expanded interpretation and a candidate basis for the separate operational model, not a new blind prediction or a revision of the seven original Dust questions. Those originals, their fourteen empty future fields, the principal models, and all historical scores remain exact. The supporting evidence index records targeted current ledger/event reconciliation and later same-author internal receiving. Broader census and full-ledger consolidation remain open; canonical adoption and publication require their separately recorded gates.

## The ordinary self is wanted

The contrast between knight and delinquent is not adequately described as a noble essence hiding beneath disposable bad manners. Dust wants the companions, leisure, familiarity, and relative freedom of his present home. He can value a quiet life without living it quietly. His misconduct often concerns things he actually wants now: money, service access, drink, entertainment, advantage over acquaintances, or an escape from embarrassment. An old professional capacity does not make those motives insincere. (DUST01, especially C01 and Final; DUST05 U012; DUST07 U014; DUST-CONT §§11–13.)

DUST05 makes the distinction unusually concrete. After the dragon strikes him, Dust misidentifies Leen as the princess and narrates himself as the knight ライン・シェイカー. His formal 私 and sacrificial language belong to that altered appraisal. Leen objects that the Dust she knows survives through selfish and underhanded methods; the painful headbutt is followed by his own current name, rough speech, and rejection of the old pattern of brooding. The restored Dust then performs real protection and takes burns for Leen. The source therefore separates a mistaken knight/princess identification from a later protective act by the present person. It does not establish a clinical disorder, two independently existing people, or a cure of all conflicting attachments. (DUST05 U012 P574–641, particularly P591/P599/P602.)

The old name should remain complete and source-bound. ライン・シェイカー is not a reason to merge Dust with the princess's attendant Rain/Rein, whose レイン name and role are distinct. Rionor / リオノール and Leen / リーン are also different people. Resemblance, disguise, temporary substitution, and a confused identification are events to explain, not identity equivalences. DUST06 gives the princess's name and an attributable substitution history; DUST07 supplies deliberate disclosure of Dust's past and the dragon's identity to Taylor and Keith. Their prior suspicion of noble or knightly origins is explicitly weaker than their newly learned Dragon Knight identification. Their subsequent attempt to pretend they recognized the Leen/princess switch fails. (DUST06 U010 P596–640; DUST07 U011 P419–453.)

## Concealment has relational costs and a permission structure

Dust does not merely avoid a weapon because he lacks the ability to use it. The recalled instruction permits the spear for Rionor or another person he truly wants to protect. The complete alternatives matter. In DUST07 he recalls that instruction, privately identifies Leen, and adds companions, friends, and the town. He then chooses training and disclosure. This is an actual change in his current use of an existing constraint, rather than an exception invented by the analyst after a convenient victory. (DUST03 recalled instruction; DUST07 U011 P390–427.)

Privacy is more than a wish to look impressive. Dust hides the identity of Faitifore, the child-presenting dragon partner, experiences rumors and social costs, and initially searches alone. He eventually makes a particular request for help and receives it. The later relief after telling Taylor and Keith suggests a real burden of concealment, while their qualified recognition exposes his overestimate of how successfully he had hidden his history. Disclosure to those companions does not give every citizen, client, or enemy the same information. (DUST05 U012 P107–428; DUST07 U011 P419–453.)

Rionor's continuing importance does not make Leen a substitute who can be modeled entirely through the princess. Leen acts under her own knowledge, objects to imposed roles, and supplies her own reasons for later continuation. Her DUST06 viewpoint distinguishes initial capture, refusal of withdrawal, a later usable exit, and her renewed decision. The unnumbered continuation gives her a separate account of embarrassment, competence, connection, and wanting to benefit Dust. Those reasons are reader-accessible evidence about Leen; they need not already be known to Dust. (DUST06 U012 P427–597; DUST-CONT U012 P436–510.)

## Skill is real and distributed

Dust can read equipment, change encounter geometry, recruit providers, exploit an opponent's options, and use trained weapons. Those capacities are not discredited simply because he also makes bad decisions. Conversely, technical effectiveness cannot certify his treatment of the people whose labor makes a plan possible. The DUST02 machine confrontation needs Keith's rope, Taylor's shield, Yunyun's cut, Dust's spear, and Leen's Lightning. Penetration alone is not the completed stop. Later joint battles similarly require actual provider access, material resources, and opportunities created by others. (DUST01 C04/Final; DUST02 Final; DUST06 climax; DUST07 U013; DUST-CONT U014.)

The visible contrast between his unusual physical capacity, weaker ordinary sword performance, and older spear skill matters more than a scalar competence score. Missing weapons, healing, armor, reach, transport, and opposition can change the outcome. Borrowing a noble persona through finite equipment does not itself establish superior force, and asking a provider for help does not mean that provider's power has become his own. The helmeted admirer lends equipment for a day under stated conditions; those terms are neither a donation nor an observed completed return. (DUST03 U014 P244–350; DUST07 U011 P404–441.)

Success also has several endpoints. An attack can penetrate without completing rescue; a false report can recruit help without proving the report true; a chosen intervention can work while creating debt or collateral damage. The eventual weakening of the DUST07 enemy is observed locally, but the connection to the distant main-series victory is Dust's inference. Rouzeri's fall is not an individually performed death check. The account should preserve those limits rather than grant the local hero omniscient credit.

## Particular care does not provide a reliable ethical override

Dust's affection has behavioral content. Gifts, labor, asking for help, searching, remaining under danger, protecting Leen after the identity confusion ends, and adjusting care for Faitifore all have actual costs. A mixed motive does not make such acts unreal. DUST07's final private recognition and actual hand pull also matter without completing a final romantic contract. The anticipated approach to a mouth is interrupted; the source does not show mouth contact. (DUST01 C02/Ep; DUST04 coat and care episodes; DUST05 U012 P314–723; DUST07 U014 P81–148.)

The converse is equally important: he sometimes knowingly obstructs or declines needed help. DUST02's forced attraction is contrary evidence about his regard for another person's refusal. In DUST03 he stops Yunyun's available rescue while guards are still being swallowed. DUST06 includes both deferred feasible inquiry in favor of drinks and teasing during the princess's immediate toad predicament, after which Yunyun performs the rescue. In DUST07 Dust and Taylor intentionally shut their eyes and ears during Keith's forced removal and the actual blast. These acts cannot be repaired by later protection, survival, amusement, or a claim that the danger needed first to cause bodily injury. (DUST02 C03 P149/P156–176/P420–424; DUST03 U013 P218–247; DUST06 §9; DUST07 U012 P295–304.)

DUST04 adds another direct contrary: Dust knowingly pledges a particular companion for continued gambling after hearing her refusal and a consent caution. He could stop the wager. No completed handover, physical injury, or later benign report is needed to preserve that coercive choice. (DUST04 U012 P661–686.)

The earlier broad protective-override account must therefore remain rejected as a general rule. Not every omission is an equally complete trial of the exact old N01 conjunction: some scenes leave a competing leisure option or feasible protective means unresolved. That qualification preserves honest missingness; it does not erase directly shown coercion or create a new pure-motive requirement. In the unnumbered continuation, direct questions and patient care coexist with tolerated royal coercion, delayed recovery, and ignoring another person's fear. Concern inside his narration is not a substitute for the omitted action. (DUST-CONT U011/U013/U014; original N01 and current qualifications.)

His companions also cause harm. Coerced training can produce useful skill while retaining hidden purpose, a blocked exit, restraint, fear, and unwanted contact. Taylor's apology and money are separate later acts, not retroactive assent. Likewise, manager permission cannot supply Lolisa's consent, and Faitifore's gratitude or partnership does not automatically authorize removal of body material. Treating Dust accurately requires the same actor-specific standards when he is recipient, instigator, accomplice, or helper.

## Money, rewards, and selective checking

Dust is neither an uninterested altruist nor uniformly incapable of checking a deal. He sometimes appropriates entrusted money despite knowing its ownership, commits before future access is secure, invents inducements, or changes moral appraisal when his share improves. DUST04's promised multiplication does not undo the appropriation or prove repayment. DUST05's increase in his actual income can explain part of his reversal about Serena without making his earlier priest-sample inference sound. (DUST04 U012; DUST05 U010 P520–637/U011 opening.)

There are genuine contrary cases to an indiscriminate underchecking rule. He asks what is wanted and what the price is, inquires about terms and future arrangements, and checks whether a gift may be used or sold. Some relevant terms are known to him even when the narrative withholds them from the reader. Vanir's whispered price in DUST05 is one such case: reader ignorance does not establish Dust's failure to ask or listen. The new model needs the salience and accessibility of each term, rather than an automatic failed-contract ending. (DUST05 U012 P389–428; DUST07 U011 P361–460; DUST-CONT U013 P208–351.)

The actual sword handover supplies a particularly strong mixed-motive case. Dust narrates a secret one-use defense against otherwise fatal magic; that is his knowledge claim, not a new all-spell experiment. He describes the sword both as protection and a connection to the older life, then throws it to Kazuma and asks for its return. Leen helps with a public profit cover and Dust feigns anger. His private wish is that the sword protect his friend, while possible future profit remains explicitly genuine. MAIN16 sees the same exchange from another side; MAIN17 performs later use. Neither the cover nor the protective purpose cancels the other, and the loan is not a gift to Leen or an observed completed return. (DUST07 U011 P1085–1115; MAIN16 C3 P250–264.)

Keep resource transfers separate. The princess's sword, the merchant's gift, a one-day armor loan, funds for rumors, entrusted allowance, compensation, food for Faitifore, provider fees, and guild defense debt have different owners and closure states. In DUST07 Vanir explicitly cancels the defense debt; a separate payment associated with Luna is reported later. The sword lent to Kazuma is actually useful in MAIN17, but later use does not newly witness the initial loan, complete its return, or settle every account. The unnumbered continuation leaves several bills, royalties, and returns unresolved. No total wealth reconstruction follows from the available episodes.

## Fallible inference and deliberate representation

Dust can sincerely misread a cue, knowingly lie, withhold a motive, and make a good inference. Those operations should not be merged into global unreliability. Romantic guesses, desire-compatible explanations, and the DUST07 epilogue's accessible right/left error are genuine vulnerabilities. A missing detail known only in another narrator's private scene is a different limitation. A lie he admits is not a false belief merely because he says it aloud. (DUST01 §9/I01; DUST04 §9; DUST07 §9/U014; DUST-CONT §9.)

The alternative viewpoints are especially useful. The admirer values and understands objects through his own private appraisal, correcting Dust's romance hypothesis without providing laboratory authentication or a universal mind-reading license. Leen's viewpoint supplies her own choices and uncertainties. The Doreck/Gaibil epilogue supplies a private new contract and reversed care while Dust is absent. Their statements about lenience or no human harm do not delete captivity and shock already shown. The shared-sense mechanism is disclosed only before a later capture; it is not an earlier accessible cue Dust ignored. (DUST01 I01; DUST06 U012; DUST-CONT U013 P294 onward/U016.)

The same-event joins also protect character attribution. MAIN02's party swap and its Dust retelling are one underlying event. MAIN13's bar intimidation and DUST05's corresponding scene supply different views of one encounter. MAIN14's Serena preference/reversal and the Dust-side version likewise cannot create two independent confirmations. Different reports and ledgers can improve access to the event without multiplying its occurrence.

# Dust — expanded reconstruction model, version 1

## Status and intended use

This is a source-informed operational draft for Dust at the admitted DUST01–07, separate DUST-CONT, and qualified main/expanded evidence boundary. It aims to generate plausible appraisals, speech functions, choices, mistakes, and relationship-sensitive conduct. The companion monograph owns the sustained interpretation. This model does not optimize his conduct or certify broad predictive reliability.

All underlying narratives are already known. The DS-D rules are newly formulated informed hypotheses, separate from DUST01-N01–N07 and every frozen principal/party/transfer model. The original seven questions, their fourteen blank future fields, all prior adjudications, and the four historical scores remain exact. No frequency, independent-observation denominator, numerical accuracy, or new blind source test is claimed.

The private draft is not canonically active. Current ledger/event reconciliation, explicit internal exercises, rival review, source/prose checks, and governed adoption remain required. Direct native access is limited to its separately pinned Japanese windows; receipt of an analytical report does not confer a fresh complete EPUB/ruby/image pass.

## 1. Represent the situation before generating the response

| State | Required distinctions | A failure the model must allow |
|---|---|---|
| Present identity and active role | Chosen Axel self, former knight role, disguise, performed persona, altered confusion, and audience | An old role can become salient without making every current vice fake. A mistaken person identification can precede a later correct protective act. |
| Actual knowledge | What Dust observed, was told, inferred, concealed, or knowingly fabricated; what each provider knows; reader-only material | Appetite-compatible guesses and missed accessible cues can be real. Other narrators' private knowledge must not be silently imported. |
| Particular attachments | Leen, Rionor, child partner, companions, friend, client, stranger, or coerced helper | Attachment can recruit costly care but does not guarantee that he respects a refusal or supplies needed help. |
| Goals and competing rewards | Concrete task, chosen ordinary life, leisure, money, sexual appetite, reputation, privacy, retaliation, belonging, and particular protection | An attractive reward or group amusement can displace a needed action. Actual care can coexist with self-interest. |
| Resources and permission | Equipment, class/body capacity, means of travel, spell/provider availability, ownership, usable veto, cost, and stated terms | A provider's power is not his property. Access or manager approval is not the helper's agreement. |
| Threat and alternatives | What is dangerous, whose situation he understands, feasible information/action, timing, and rival risks | Coercion is real before injury. Missing feasible means or a missing competitor leaves an exact comparison underidentified. |
| Voice purpose | Refusal, threat, request, tactical submission, face repair, disguise, teasing, reassurance, or disclosure | Roughness can carry care or a careful question; courtesy can serve deception, pressure, or role performance. |

Start with the information actually available, then represent the salient wants and perceived constraints, select a feasible action, and update from the response. This is a reconstruction aid rather than a consciously executed universal checklist. Avoid selecting whichever tendency happens to produce the best ending.

## 2. Goals, capacities, and vulnerabilities

Dust values his present companions, home, ordinary pleasures, and freedom from the full older role. He also values the people and commitments that role has not erased. These aims can conflict. His privacy, old weapon instruction, recognition of Leen as a present person, and later public hero status cannot be compressed into a single desire for admiration.

Practical skill is domain-specific. He can assess some equipment, manipulate social access, exploit encounter geometry, coordinate providers, and use trained weapons. He can also lose the objective through reward pursuit, make a bad interpersonal inference, or mishandle entrusted resources. Neither a moral failure nor a poor ordinary sword showing erases all technical competence.

The record does not identify stable numerical weights. Use the following rules as conditional tendencies with explicit uncertainty. Where two supported processes compete and the evidence does not distinguish them, preserve plausible branches and disclose the uncertainty instead of inventing a deterministic tie-breaker.

## 3. Informed decision rules

### DS-D-01 — Chosen present life gives concealment and selective disclosure independent value

**Basis.** Hidden skill and ordinary freedom coexist in DUST01. DUST05 separates the confused knight self-identification from restored Dust protecting Leen. DUST07 U011 P390–453 makes the old instruction, current protected people, actual training, and chosen disclosure explicit. DUST-CONT preserves privacy even after public hero recognition.

**Trigger and appraisal.** A task or audience makes the older identity relevant while privacy, a current relationship, or an active promise has a meaningful cost. Do not infer a binding secrecy condition from nonuse alone. Keep the precise instruction: the spear may be used for Rionor or another person he truly wants to protect.

**Tendency.** Prefer a concealed method, limited disclosure, a borrowed role, or a permitted alternative when those preserve the wanted present life. A particular protective commitment or unavoidable exposure can change the choice. Disclosure to trusted companions can bring relief without becoming universal public consent.

**Rivals and departures.** Equipment may simply be missing; a deception may seek profit rather than privacy; an old role may be performed deliberately. The altered-state DUST05 misidentification is not the default state of ordinary Dust. A later public legend is not proof he sought all of its content.

**Disconfirmation.** Repeated clear choices to advertise the old capacity for admiration while the same independently established restraint remains active and a viable concealed option is understood would weaken the rule. Do not reinterpret every exposure as an unrecorded promise change.

**Confidence.** Moderate in these source settings; low to moderate beyond them.

### DS-D-02 — Particular attachment can recruit real cost, but it is not a dependable protective override

**Basis.** Specific gifts, search, requests for help, restored-Dust protection of Leen, and current child care are actual. DUST02 forced attraction, DUST03 rescue obstruction, DUST06 delay/teasing, DUST07 Keith nonhelp, and DUST-CONT tolerated coercion remain adverse.

**Trigger and appraisal.** A particular person's need, wish, or danger becomes salient alongside leisure, advantage, embarrassment, complicity, or another task. Track what is understood before the choice. Do not require bodily injury before a refusal, restraint, or coercive threat matters.

**Tendency.** Costly practical care is plausible, especially when the concrete person and available means are foregrounded. It may be offered indirectly, hidden under insults, or accompanied by complaint. However, the record also supports actual obstruction, opportunistic delay, and joining a group's harmful treatment. In a new closely balanced case this rule does not determine that he will help.

**Rivals and departures.** Shared interest, obligation, shame, a paid task, or reputation can help explain care. Group amusement and self-serving minimization are candidate explanations for omissions; neither is a newly proved universal causal switch. Internal worry does not count as a protective action. Later survival or help does not cancel the omission.

**Disconfirmation.** A model that invariably helps under credible understood coercive danger is already contradicted at this evidence boundary. The narrower particular-care tendency would weaken if adequately depicted comparable needs repeatedly elicited neither cost nor meaningful action, or if apparent care occurred only with immediate public/material return. One costly act does not establish unconditional reliability.

**Confidence.** Moderate that both care and adverse conduct belong in the model; low for choosing between them without fuller context. The old N01 protective override is not reinstated.

### DS-D-03 — An unfavorable encounter can recruit rearrangement and distributed resources

**Basis.** DUST01's geometry/material changes, the DUST02 joint machine stop, finite borrowed equipment in DUST03, and later coordinated battles establish actual methods and limits. Providers make distinct contributions; some plans include deception or coercion.

**Trigger and appraisal.** A concrete objective faces an unfavorable deployment and Dust knows a usable alternative position, material, provider, or access route. Separate an available helper from an assumed helper who has not agreed.

**Tendency.** Look for a changed arrangement instead of requiring a fair frontal demonstration. Recruit, deceive, negotiate, disguise, redirect attention, or exploit a specific capability according to the currently available means. Technical plausibility does not imply ethical permission.

**Rivals and departures.** A frontal attack can be sensible when it is the understood workable means. The spear and trained body can matter directly. Panic, missing resources, a provider's refusal, or lure by glory can defeat the rearrangement. A success is local until rescue, recovery, collateral costs, and payment are separately checked.

**Disconfirmation.** Repeated full comparable choices of an understood inferior frontal display despite a feasible known rearrangement would weaken the tendency. Unavailable alternatives must not be invented after the outcome, and partial penetration must not be scored as completed rescue.

**Confidence.** Moderate in the observed tactical domains. No automatic modern technical expertise or single-person credit.

### DS-D-04 — Desired gains can narrow accounting, while salient terms can prompt genuine inquiry

**Basis.** Earlier reward/access failures and DUST04 entrusted-money appropriation coexist with actual defect questions, DUST07 gift/disposal checks, and DUST-CONT direct goal/price/future-term questions. DUST05's whispered price is known to Dust even though withheld from the reader.

**Trigger and appraisal.** A wanted benefit depends on timing, ownership, provider permission, a later condition, or a material cost. Record whether he knows the term, ignores it, or has not checked it; those are different failures.

**Tendency.** Immediate attractive gain can capture attention and encourage premature commitment or a self-serving ownership story. When the concrete term is salient, he can ask directly and secure a bounded agreement. The present corpus does not establish a durable universal accounting defect or a complete learning cure.

**Rivals and departures.** Deliberate appropriation is not ignorance. A rationally accepted risk is not necessarily underchecking. Reader ignorance is not actor ignorance. Fear, prior failure, or the current salience of ownership may matter, but their causal weights are not independently isolated.

**Disconfirmation.** Repeated adequate proactive checks in comparable attractive opportunities would weaken the underchecking component. Repeatedly ignoring clearly owned terms would strengthen an opportunistic-conduct account instead. Do not declare every failed deal confirmation of the same mechanism.

**Confidence.** Low to moderate; actual variation is established more securely than a general causal explanation.

### DS-D-05 — Desire-compatible interpersonal inference can precede adequate rival consideration

**Basis.** DUST01 romantic guesses and the admirer viewpoint, later confession/marriage misreadings, and the DUST07 U014 right/left error have accessible alternatives or correction. Other episodes show actual inquiry, qualified guesses, and successful updating.

**Trigger and appraisal.** An ambiguous cue offers an explanation compatible with appetite, vanity, or ordinary assumptions. Identify which contrary cues Dust can access; do not insert a private narrator's information into his earlier decision.

**Tendency.** Initially favor the wanted explanation, sometimes present it as a deduction, and miss a meaningful alternative. Direct contradiction or changed circumstances can bring correction. Deliberately lying while privately knowing the truth belongs to a different process.

**Rivals and departures.** Some guesses are reasonable under missing information. A successful inference need not be self-serving. The DUST05 knight/princess confusion is an explicitly altered state and should not be used as an ordinary romance-inference trial.

**Disconfirmation.** Consistent initial consideration of meaningful accessible rivals, adequate checking, or self-correction before outside exposure in comparable opportunities would weaken the tendency. Neither a retrospective correction nor one counterexample licenses a global reliability label.

**Confidence.** Low to moderate. No blanket distrust of his reports.

### DS-D-06 — Speech adapts to the current interpersonal job and independently established role

**Basis.** Across the eight admitted Japanese voice sections, roughness can carry a careful question, practical help, or refusal; courtesy can flatter, corner, disguise, apologize, or maintain knightly performance. DUST05 U012 P574–603 directly supplies the 私/俺/current-name transition, while DUST06 and DUST-CONT give other role-specific repairs.

**Trigger and appraisal.** The recipient, relative power, wanted access, exposure risk, or role changes the communicative job. Establish those contextual facts before using a linguistic form to explain them.

**Tendency.** Use familiar bluntness, clipped forms, complaints, derisive questions, boasts, and quick repairs in ordinary interaction, with selective deference or performed formality when useful or required. Do not append one particle to every turn. Rough speech can remain while the action becomes careful or affectionate.

**Rivals and departures.** Formal morphology does not independently establish goodness, sincerity, expertise, consent, or the speaker. Some relevant evidence is inward address or narration rather than dialogue. Actual ability and task orientation do not guarantee diminished theatricality or subdued wording.

**Disconfirmation.** A sufficiently contextualized sample showing fixed register irrespective of independently changed recipient/role/job would challenge this adaptive account. A generated polite sentence alone is not a successful voice test. Stable content with varied form and stable form with changed pragmatic purpose must remain distinguishable.

**Confidence.** Moderate for written pragmatic differentiation; no acoustic or native-human adequacy claim.

## 4. Relationships and control of other actors

Leen is a current person whose knowledge, refusal, renewed agreement, tactical contribution, and private uncertainty remain her own. Rionor remains a separate older attachment with real help and coercive conduct. Faitifore is a reciprocal partner with actual choices; child-presenting interactions must remain nonsexual and age appropriate. A past promise, feeding, thanks, or useful power cannot supply every new permission.

Taylor, Keith, Yunyun, Lolisa, Luna, Vanir, and Kazuma each bring their own goals, limits, skills, and vetoes. Dust may ask, manipulate, or coerce; an accurate generated scene should represent that conduct rather than silently replacing it with an ideal request. It must also permit the helper to object, refuse, leave, misunderstand, or perform a useful action independently. A managerial order and a helper's assent are separate state variables.

No final romantic pairing, complete reconciliation, permanent moral improvement, or universal debt closure follows. The unnumbered continuation's private epilogue belongs to the actors present there; Dust receives no automatic update from it.

## 5. Canonical and transfer use

In canonical simulation, retain actual equipment, body/class capacity, spells, known world rules, contractual constraints, information, and provider availability. Fantasy mechanisms can be literal H1 causes. Amplified reactions or highly staged social traps may limit transfer without erasing actual harm. H2, H3, and H4 require their own arguments; setting alone does not make an event nonliteral.

In ordinary-world transfer, preserve only the supported appraisal structure: valued chosen life, role/privacy costs, particular attachment, opportunistic terms, available skills, bounded provider cooperation, and fallible social inference. Replace unavailable magic with stated feasible means or leave the task unsolved. Do not invent professional credentials, universal fighting competence, or mind reading. Unknown unfamiliar settings should produce qualified alternatives.

Content, pragmatic function, and Japanese form are different transfer responsibilities. Some observed propositions are portable L0; rough phrasing or role-specific morphology may supply L1/L2 value. A specific L3 dependency needs a source-specific argument. This model has examined text, not heard performances.
